deck: Table Rock this morning: 909.80 ft. Taneycomo still eats on a pink worm if the generators give you a window.

play.title: Fish the wind.
play.body: Fall bass set up where the shad get blown. A crankbait that bangs is better than a worm that sits.

season.name: Fall turnover
season.why: The lake turns over and the fish don't read the same book they did in August. Crankbaits get good again. Trout streamers get good. This is the season Branson locals wait for.
tips: Windblown banks and shad-colored cranks, 8–18 feet.
Walleye on the same gravel they used all summer, just shallower.
Taneycomo: streamers and wooly buggers when they generate. Hoppers until the first frost.
A jacket in the boat. Dawn is cold before the strip is.

tomorrow: Tomorrow we print a new level, a new play, and whether the dam spun overnight. Open it before you drive. The water will have moved.
weekGraf: The pool walked down from 910.27 early in the week to 909.77 this morning — about 0.5 ft off that earlier mark, still under the 915 full pool. Live USACE reading 10:00 CT: 909.77 ft, 9,148 cfs through the dam. Ramps are still in. Shallow coves feel a falling pool first.

now.temp: Verify at the ramp — scout does not invent dawn temps
now.clarity: Clear near the dam; arms can stain. Verify locally.

body: At 909.80 ft this morning the lake sits more than 5 ft below full pool. Exposed shoreline, shallow coves, and longer walks at some ramps are the norm — use caution in the James, Kings, and Long Creek arms where hazards sit closer to the surface.

Surface water has cooled into the low-to-mid 50s °F with exceptional clarity. Bass are hitting topwaters and soft plastics in low light before transitioning to jigs, live bait, or drop-shot presentations around long points, gravel flats dropping into deeper water, and offshore structure. Walleye and crappie continue producing around brush piles and points. In this clear, cooling water, clean natural presentations win the day for anglers dialed into the fall transition.

taneycomo.dek: Cold tailwater · generation is the whole game

now.temp: Tailwater cold (typically ~50–54°F below the dam). Verify at the bank.
now.generation: ~9,148 cfs at 10:00 CT (USACE live). Call SWPA 866-494-1993 before you wad.

body: This cold tailwater remains one of the most consistent trout fisheries in the Midwest thanks to steady MDC stocking and cold releases from the bottom of Table Rock Dam. Generation is the primary tactic book: low or no generation allows lighter rigs, wading, or indicator fishing in the seams and soft water; stronger flows (such as the 81–150 MW pulses shown on today's SWPA schedule) demand added weight, drifting the current breaks, and 2–4 lb test.

From Table Rock Dam down to Fall Creek is trophy water — artificial lures and flies only; no soft plastics or scented/natural baits allowed. Rainbows 12–20 inches must be released. Save pink worms, PowerBait, or other soft plastics/scented baits for water below Fall Creek. A trout permit is required in many areas. Recent reports show solid numbers of rainbows with increasing brown trout activity in the upper stretches on marabou jigs, midges, scuds, small streamers, and eggs. Water clarity is generally excellent. Always call 866-494-1993 for the latest SWPA generation schedule before heading out and stay clear of the closed zone below the dam.

editor.note: Two-lake daily rebuilt from the morning fishing scout plus the prior week of files. We print a level only when the scout had one. Carry-forward mornings are labeled. No invented bite ratings. Call 866-494-1993 before wading Taneycomo.
